Fit an intercept correction on a recalibration sample

Source: R/recalibrate.R
mm_recal_intercept.Rd

Fits y ~ offset(lp), so the model's linear predictor is held fixed and the constant is the only free parameter. A positive value means the model predicts too low.

Usage

mm_recal_intercept(lp, y, cluster = NULL, positive = NULL)

Arguments

lp

Linear predictors from the FROZEN model, not refitted here. For an mm_model() these are fitted(model, scale = "link") on new rows.

y

The observed outcome, in any form mm_model() accepts.

cluster

An identifier for rows that are not independent, or NULL.

positive

The level that means the event, as in mm_project().

Value

A list: a, se, n, events, cluster_robust, n_clusters, and a one-line reason.

Details

The standard error is cluster-robust when cluster is supplied and the sandwich package is installed. When one patient contributes more than one row, a model-based standard error treats those rows as independent and is too small; the returned cluster_robust flag says which was used, rather than leaving a caller to assume.

Examples

cohort <- mm_synthetic_cohort(n = 400, seed = 9)
fit <- suppressWarnings(mm_model(
  mm_project("recal", "event", c("age", "bmi"),
             positive_class = 1, cohort = cohort), cohort))
lp <- as.numeric(fit$fit$linear.predictors)
mm_recal_intercept(lp, cohort$event, positive = 1)$reason
#> [1] "intercept correction +0.0000 (SE 0.1680, model-based, rows treated as independent) from 400 rows, 40 event(s) (10.0%)"
